The image presents two bar graphs, one for Germany and one for the EU, illustrating the percentage of various metals (Aluminium, Kupfer/Copper, and Nickel) in 2021, 2022, and 2023. The graphs feature a blue bar for 2021, a purple bar for 2022, and a grey bar for 2023. The y-axis represents the percentage, ranging from 0 to 30% in increments of 5%, while the x-axis lists the metals.

In the Germany graph, Aluminium accounts for 3.6% in 2021, 2.7% in 2022, and 1% in 2023. Kupfer/Copper makes up 8.3% in 2021, 11.3% in 2022, and 2.2% in 2023. Nickel constitutes 25.1% in 2021, 24.7% in 2022, and 11.4% in 2023.

In the EU graph, Aluminium represents 3.2% in 2021, 2.8% in 2022, and 1.7% in 2023. Kupfer/Copper comprises 4.4% in 2021, 5.1% in 2022, and 1.3% in 2023. Nickel accounts for 24.3% in 2021, 23.3% in 2022, and 14.6% in 2023.

The graphs provide a clear visual representation of the trends and changes in the percentages of these metals over the three-year period, allowing for a comparison between Germany and the EU.
